units.name: Late Amazonian polar dunes unit
units.char: Mounds with barchan-like, linear, and other dune morphologies. Low albedo. Marked by meter-scale ripples. Mounds typically tens to hundreds of meters across and tens of meters high. (lat 81.21° N., long 217.34° E.)
units.interp: Wind-blown sand organized into variety of dune forms owing to variable wind activity and permafrost development

units.name: Amazonian polar unit
units.char: Plainsforming deposit. Relatively low radar dielectric constant. As much as 1,000 m thick. (lat –76.62° N., long 287.50° E.)
units.interp: Dominantly water ice and minor lithic fines; pits may be thermokarst forms produced in part by magmatism

units.name: Late Amazonian polar cap unit
units.char: Hummocky and pitted at meter (northern cap) to hundreds of meter (southern cap) scales. Very high albedo except on pit floors. Mostly <2 m (northern cap) to <10 m (southern cap) thick. (lat 83.00° N., long 317.85° E. and lat –86.04° N., long 291.81° E.)
units.interp: Residual ice (H2O in northern cap and mainly CO2 in southern cap) with dust lags trapped in north polar pits. Margins and surface of unit actively changing due to ice accumulation and ablation

units.name: Hesperian polar edifice unit
units.char: Shields and cones having summit and flank depressions in polar regions. Relatively low radar dielectric constant. Hundreds of meters thick. (lat 75.94° N., long 206.23° E. and lat –75.96° N., long 341.69° E.)
units.interp: Cryovolcanic or sedimentary or igneous volcanic, ice-rich constructs. Highly degraded by mass wasting and (or) sublimation

units.name: Hesperian polar undivided unit
units.char: Plateau-forming deposits. Decameter-thick layers. Relatively low radar dielectric constant. Locally >1,000 m thick. (lat 80.28° N., long 302.72° E.)
units.interp: Roughly equal proportions of water ice and lithic fines, possibly emplaced during lowland flooding events or by eolian activity. Deeply eroded but armored by impact material; lower sequence troughed likely due to compaction

units.name: Hesperian polar unit
units.char: Plains-forming deposits marked by narrow sinuous, anabranching ridges and irregular depressions. Relatively low radar dielectric constant. Hundreds of meters thick. (lat –77.78° N., long 332.51° E.; locality 48)
units.interp: Water-ice sheets as indicated by dielectric constant, perhaps emplaced by cryovolcanism or from atmospheric precipitation. Covered by thin, periglacially deformed mantling deposit

units.name: Amazonian polar undivided unit
units.char: Plateaus hundreds of kilometers across at both poles. Moderate to high albedo. Meters-thick layers; some internal unconformities; local lower, mostly low-albedo deposits unevenly bedded or crossbedded. Exceeds 1,000 m thickness in places. (lat 80.97° N., long 0.00° E. and lat –83.15° N., long 64.91° E.)
units.interp: Water ice with minor amounts of dust intermixed and as lags; local lower sequences made up of frozen dunes with interbedded ice layers

units.name: Late Hesperian volcanic field unit
units.char: Patches hundreds of kilometers across of lobate flows typically meters thick and tens of kilometers long emanating from low shields and fissure vents kilometers to tens of kilometers across. Hundreds of meters or more total thickness. (lat –12.31° N., long 257.63° E.)
units.interp: Volcanoes and lava flows

units.name: Amazonian volcanic edifice
units.char: Shieldlike edifices hundreds of kilometers across; made up of lobate flows meters to tens of meters thick and tens to hundreds of kilometers across. Edifices several to more than ten kilometers high. (lat 18.89° N., long 225.86° E.)
units.interp: Volcanic edifices composed of lava flows and possible volcaniclastic rocks. Deformed by summit collapse from magma withdrawal and gravity spreading of flanks

units.name: Late Noachian volcanic unit
units.char: Planar deposits meters to tens of meters thick and tens to hundreds of kilometers across; lobate scarps sparse and indistinct. Variable daytime IR brightness in places. Hundreds of meters or more total thickness. (lat –55.89° N., long 67.99° E.; localities 46, 47)
units.interp: Degraded lava and volcaniclastic flows. Tectonically contracted

units.name: Early Hesperian volcanic unit
units.char: Planar deposits meters to tens of meters thick and tens to hundreds of kilometers across; lobate scarps common. Variable daytime IR brightness in places. Hundreds of meters or more total thickness. (lat –25.34° N., long 279.97° E.; localities 38, 42)
units.interp: Flood lavas, undifferentiated, sourced from regional fissure and vent systems. Tectonically contracted

units.name: Noachian volcanic edifice unit
units.char: Shield-like edifices several tens to hundreds of kilometers across; lobate flow morphologies indistinct or absent. As much as few kilometers thick. (lat –8.11° N., long 174.50° E.)
units.interp: Volcanic edifices composed of different combinations of lava flows, pyroclastic deposits, and volcaniclastic deposits sourced from degraded shields. Domed and fractured by local intrusions. Tectonically contracted

units.name: Amazonian and Hesperian volcanic
units.char: Stacked, gently sloping lobate flows meters to tens of meters thick and hundreds of kilometers long. Variable daytime IR brightness in places. Cumulative thicknesses reach hundreds of meters to several kilometers. (lat –22.76° N., long 242.33° E.)
units.interp: Flood lavas and large lava flows, undifferentiated, sourced from regional fissure and vent systems. Highly variable ages of individual flows, although generally younger in central parts of Tharsis rise

units.name: Late Amazonian volcanic field unit
units.char: Flows each typically tens of kilometers long extending from shields and fissure vents as much as tens of kilometers across. Meters to at least tens of meters thick. (lat –2.13° N., long 253.85° E.)
units.interp: Largely unmodified lava flows and vents; vents and flows not differentiated at map scale

units.name: Late Amazonian volcanic unit
units.char: Planar deposits containing lobate scarps that extend hundreds to more than 1,000 km; sinuous troughs, ridges, and platy textures common; low-relief, shield-like edifices rare. Meters to tens of meters thick. (lat 26.27° N., long 192.67° E.; localities 9, 21)
units.interp: Largely unmodified flood lavas, including lava channels and other morphologies; sourced from fissures and shields

units.name: Hesperian volcanic edifice unit
units.char: Shield-like edifices several tens to hundreds of kilometers across; made up of lobate flows meters to tens of meters thick and tens to hundreds of kilometers across, as well as dissected layers tens of meters thick. As much as few kilometers thick. (lat 24.65° N., long 146.80° E.)
units.interp: Volcanic edifices composed of different combinations of lava flows and pyroclastic and volcaniclastic deposits. Modified by summit collapse from magma withdrawal and fluvial dissection in places

units.name: Amazonian volcanic unit
units.char: Rugged, hummocky, and pitted fields of irregular, poorly defined flows forming plains hundreds to more than 1,000 km across. Tens of meters or more thick. (lat 34.82° N., long 135.11° E.; locality 4)
units.interp: Lava and perhaps volcaniclastic flows from Elysium Mons and unknown source northwest of Olympus Mons

units.name: Late Hesperian volcanic unit
units.char: Lobate flows, meters to tens of meters thick and tens to hundreds of kilometers long; forms patches hundreds to more than a thousand kilometers across. Variable daytime IR brightness in places. Hundreds of meters or more total thickness. (lat –18.84° N., long 256.12° E.; localities 17, 29)
units.interp: Flood lavas and large lava flows, undifferentiated, sourced from regional fissure and vent systems

units.name: Early Noachian highland massif unit
units.char: High-relief massifs tens of kilometers across separated by broad linear troughs and valleys. Kilometers thick. (lat –44.48° N., long 307.54° E.)
units.interp: Ancient, degraded crustal rocks uplifted by large, basin-forming impacts. Dissected by basin-related fault structures and erosional valleys

units.name: Middle Noachian highland massif unit
units.char: High-relief massifs tens of kilometers across separated by broad linear troughs and valleys. Kilometers thick. (lat –44.48° N., long 307.54° E.)
units.interp: Ancient, degraded crustal rocks uplifted by large, basin-forming impacts. Dissected by basin-related fault structures and erosional valleys

units.name: Early Amazonian basin unit
units.char: Plainsforming deposits on basin floor; hummocky and troughed textures. Variable daytime IR brightness. Thickness <100 m in most places. (lat 37.44° N., long 111.17° E.; localities 3, 5, 41)
units.interp: Lacustrine and (or) sheet-flood deposits. Perhaps modified by compaction and thermokarst

units.name: Late Hesperian basin unit
units.char: Plainsforming deposits on basin floor. Finely layered in places. Hundreds of meters thick. (lat –40.80° N.,  long 64.00° E.; locality 39)
units.interp: Ice-rich eolian, lacustrine, and (or) volcanic air-fall deposits. Margins eroded and back-wasted

units.name: Early Hesperian basin unit
units.char: Plainsforming deposit. Several hundred meters thick along contact with unit HNb. (lat –37.95° N., long 78.84° E.; locality 44)
units.interp: Basin fill of eolian, lacustrine, and (or) volcanic origin. Modified by fluvial dissection. Tectonically contracted

units.name: Hesperian and Noachian basin unit
units.char: Low-lying, plains-forming deposit. Relatively low daytime IR brightness in Hellas Planitia. Thickness at least hundreds of meters. (lat –33.53° N., long 59.53° E.; locality 40)
units.interp: Basin fill of eolian, lacustrine, and (or) volcanic origin. Tectonically contracted. Sinuous ridges in Argyre Planitia interpreted as inverted fluvial landforms or eskers

units.name: Middle Amazonian lowland unit
units.char: Hummocky to undulating; grades into fields of knobs. Internally stratified. Tens of meters thick. (lat 51.43° N., long 118.45° E.)
units.interp: Ice-rich loess. Periglacial modification formed thumbprint terrain

units.name: Late Hesperian lowland unit
units.char: Planar to undulating; lobate and troughed marginal areas in places. Hundreds of meters to kilometers thick. (lat 21.40° N., long 118.20° E.; localities 1, 6, 10, 11)
units.interp: Fluvial/lacustrine/marine and colluvial sediments sourced from circum-lowland outflow channels and bounding highland terrains; likely intercalated with and underlain by lava and volcaniclastic rocks. Pervasively modified and obscured by periglaciation, sedimentary diapirism, and particulate mantling

units.name: Late Hesperian transition unit
units.char: Plains-forming deposits, relatively smooth; includes small knobs and mesas of Noachian and perhaps younger material. May be tens to hundreds of meters thick. (lat 18.13° N., long 117.11° E.; localities 8, 15)
units.interp: Mass-wasting, fluvial/lacustrine, and possibly other sedimentary materials and volcanic rocks in places. Tectonically contracted

units.name: Hesperian transition outflow unit
units.char: Plains deposits in places dissected by tens-of-kilometers-wide anabranching channel systems. Relatively bright in nighttime IR in Maja Valles. Meters to at least tens of meters thick. (lat 19.33° N., long 326.45° E.—Mars Pathfinder landing site; locality 12)
units.interp: Outflow channel fluvial and debris-flow deposits from catastrophic erosion of highland rocks; islands of underlying bedrock exposed

units.name: Hesperian transition unit
units.char: Knobs, mesas, and intervening aprons and plains within highland canyons and chaotic terrain. Hundreds of meters thick. (lat 1.75° N., long 325.45° E.)
units.interp: Mixture of sediments and blocks of broken up, mass-wasted, and collapsed materials

units.name: Early Hesperian transition unit
units.char: Plains-forming deposits, undulating to moderately rugged; includes scattered low knobs and mesas of Noachian highland material. May be tens to hundreds of meters thick. (lat 13.38° N., long 116.70° E.; localities 2, 16)
units.interp: Mass-wasting, fluvial/lacustrine, and other sedimentary materials and possibly volcanic rocks in places. Tectonically contracted

units.name: Amazonian and Hesperian transition undivided unit
units.char: Irregularly shaped plateaus hundreds to more than one thousand kilometers across. Locally layered. Hundreds of meters to ~3,000 m thick.  (lat –2.37° N., long 240.33° E.; localities 25, 27, 30)
units.interp: Fine-grained eolian sediments and (or) pyroclastic air-fall deposits. Linear ridges and grooves form yardangs

units.name: Hesperian and Noachian transition unit
units.char: Knobs, mesas, and intervening aprons and plains. May be tens to hundreds of meters thick. (lat 10.96° N., long 111.71° E.; locality 18)
units.interp: Noachian impact breccias, sediments, and volcanic deposits with intervening aprons of Hesperian mass-wasted materials. Tectonically contracted

units.name: Hesperian transition undivided unit
units.char: Irregular plateaus hundreds of kilometers across. Layered. Hundreds of meters to kilometers thick. (lat –6.41° N., long 156.42° E; lat –6.17° N., long 286.05° E.; localities 26, 28)
units.interp: Fine-grained eolian sediments and (or) pyroclastic air-fall deposits. Modified by fluvial dissection and eolian erosion. Linear ridges and grooves form yardangs. Tectonically contracted. Channels mostly inverted. Altered by acidic weathering in places

units.name: Middle Noachian highland unit
units.char: Uneven to rolling topography; high-relief outcrops that extend hundreds to thousands of kilometers. Commonly layered in crater walls. May be hundreds of meters to more than a kilometer thick. (lat –47.17° N., long 349.33° E.; localities 7, 14, 19, 20, 22, 23, 31)
units.interp: Undifferentiated impact, volcanic, fluvial, and basin materials. Moderately to heavily degraded

units.name: Late Noachian highland unit
units.char: Mostly plains forming, rugged in places. May be hundreds of meters thick. (lat –20.74° N., long 354.35° E.; localities 13, 34, 35)
units.interp: Undifferentiated impact, volcanic, fluvial, and basin material. Lightly to heavily degraded and (or) deformed

units.name: Early Hesperian highland unit
units.char: High plains-forming, relatively smooth outcrops extending hundreds of kilometers. May be hundreds of meters thick. (lat 15.88° N., long 293.44° E.)
units.interp: Undifferentiated impact, volcanic, eolian, fluvial/lacustrine materials. Locally degraded and (or) deformed

units.name: Early Noachian highland unit
units.char: Rugged, very high relief outcrops extending hundreds of kilometers. Thickness commonly exceeds a few kilometers but ill-defined. (lat –20.74° N., long 354.35° E; localities 33, 36)
units.interp: Undifferentiated impact, volcanic, fluvial, and basin materials. Heavily degraded; tectonically deformed in places

units.name: Noachian highland edifice unit
units.char: Irregular edifices marked by troughs and peaks. As much as a few kilometers thick. (lat –34.72° N., long 214.85° E.)
units.interp: Mainly undifferentiated, degraded volcanic materials. Heavily degraded and tectonically modified

units.name: Noachian highland undivided unit
units.char: Forms canyon walls and some high plains and channel floors. Layered. Hundreds of meters to several kilometers thick in exposures. (lat –25.80° N., long 288.53° E.; locality 37)
units.interp: Undifferentiated friable sedimentary, impact, and volcanic materials. Tectonically contracted in places

units.name: Hesperian and Noachian highland undivided unit
units.char: Mound forming. Light toned in visible images. Layered. Hundreds of meters to several kilometers thick. (lat 5.97° N., long 2.33° E.; locality 24)
units.interp: Undifferentiated, friable (likely fine grained) sedimentary, volcanic, and impact rocks. Altered by weathering

units.name: Amazonian apron unit
units.char: Lobes bounded by scarps tens to hundreds of kilometers across, marked by transverse ridges few kilometers wide and tens of kilometers long; linear grooves in places. As much as 1,000 m thick. (lat –8.04° N., long 281.80° E. and lat 30.17° N., long 214.65° E.)
units.interp: Landslide and gravity-spreading deposits derived from flanks of Olympus Mons and walls of Valles Marineris

units.name: Amazonian and Noachian apron unit
units.char: Irregular knobs and mesas tens of kilometers across and aprons extending tens of kilometers from them. Aprons hundreds of meters thick. (lat –43.22° N., long 26.66° E.)
units.interp: Ice-rich Amazonian materials derived from air-fall and mass-wasting erosion and transported by mass flow and underlying, relict Noachian highland materials. Modified by thermokarst processes

units.name: Late Amazonian apron unit
units.char: Concentrically ribbed, knobby lobes extending as much as 500 km from shield-like edifices. Meters (or less) to tens-of-meters thick. (lat 4.33° N., long 243.07° E.)
units.interp: Drop moraines left by cold-based glaciers

units.name: Amazonian and Hesperian impact unit
units.char: Craters with rims and surrounding blankets; some include single to multi-lobed blanket forms, dense secondary crater chains, and (or) central peak or pit. Blanket thicknesses of meters to a few hundred meters. (lat 23.17° N., long 207.77° E.
units.interp: Upturned, ejected, and brecciated target rocks and sediments, with local areas of impact melt. Post-impact mass-wasting and fluvial-lacustrine and eolian infill of craters common
